domain: volatility-shape and cross-sectional risk-state information from daily OHLCV (assigned A4 column)

mechanism.causal_economic_mechanism: Cross-sectional pricing of UNCERTAINTY ABOUT RISK, distinct from the risk level itself. For each sector ETF, volatility-of-volatility (vov) is the dispersion of the asset's own rolling realized-volatility path: the sample standard deviation of 12 consecutive non-overlapping 21-session realized volatilities over the trailing 252 sessions. The literature documents a robust negative cross-sectional relation: assets whose future risk is hard to predict earn LOWER subsequent returns than stable-risk assets - Baltussen, van Bekkum & van der Grient document this 'unknown unknowns' effect across stocks worldwide and show it is not absorbed by the volatility level or established factors; the market-level variance-risk strand (Bollerslev-Tauchen-Zhou) independently shows that state variables describing the uncertainty of the risk process carry return-predictive information, and the volatility-level strand (Ang-Hodrick-Xing-Zhang) provides the level benchmark that the vov claim must be separated from. Economic reading: investors with vol-based mandates, risk limits and leverage constraints concentrate in assets whose risk is stable and predictable, bidding those up, while assets with erratic risk paths are neglected or held at a discount - so uncertainty about risk, not just risk, is priced. The tradable, falsifiable form in sector space: a market-neutral spread LONG the 3 lowest-vov sectors and SHORT the 3 highest-vov sectors should earn positive expectancy. Whether this single-name anomaly transfers to 11 large liquid sector composites is exactly the open question the anchor tests.
mechanism.why_after_cost_information_should_surviv: The arm is market-neutral (gross <= 1.2, net ~ 0) with a quarterly-persistent state variable: a 12-month vov estimate moves slowly, so with a 21-session decision clock, hysteresis entry/exit bands and static weights between ticks, expected turnover is ~0.8-2.0 two-way per year (point estimate ~1.3, ~15-35% of the frozen 6.0 ceiling), a cost drag of ~13 bps/year at the 10 bps base and ~26 bps at the 20 bps stress. Documented single-name vov spreads are of order 1-4% per year; even substantial attenuation at the composite level would clear that drag. Market-direction exposure is absent by construction (net ~ 0, sign-free second-moment signal) and again removed by the frozen risk-matched SPY-context subtraction and the sector-factor intercept, so surviving expectancy is not SPY/sector beta and not 'long when trend up': no price-level trend, moving average or vol-target rotation input exists anywhere in the design.
mechanism.falsifiable_prediction: Directional and specific: the anchor spread (long the 3 lowest volatility-of-volatility sectors, short the 3 highest, market-neutral, hysteresis book, 21-session clock) has strictly positive expectancy after 10 bps/side base costs, positive incremental alpha versus the risk-matched SPY context overall, and risk-matched excess return in at least 2 of 3 folds. If the spread is positive but the realized-vol LEVEL control reproduces it at ratio >= 0.5 (the claim is then the low-vol level anomaly, not risk-uncertainty pricing), or if the stable sign is opposite, the anchor is rejected as specified - no post-hoc sign rescue and no window tweak.

primary_sources: Baltussen, van Bekkum & van der Grient (2018), 'Unknown Unknowns: Uncertainty About Risk and Stock Returns', Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis 53(3) - stocks with high volatility-of-volatility earn reliably lower subsequent returns worldwide; the direct mechanism citation for this anchor's direction

Bollerslev, Tauchen & Zhou (2009), 'Expected Stock Returns and Variance Risk Premia', Review of Financial Studies 22(11): 4463-4492 - state variables of the risk-uncertainty process carry return-predictive information at the market level

Ang, Hodrick, Xing & Zhang (2006), 'The Cross-Section of Volatility and Expected Returns', Journal of Finance 61(1): 259-299 - the volatility-LEVEL benchmark; cited as the basis of the level-sort negative control the vov claim must be separated from

fields_used: for each of the 11 sector ETFs (XLB, XLC, XLE, XLF, XLI, XLK, XLP, XLRE, XLU, XLV, XLY): {SYM}_all_p1.json values[].datetime and values[].close (split+dividend adjusted) - sole signal and return input; daily total returns and block realized volatilities are close-to-close on the adjusted path
SPY_all_p1.json values[].datetime and values[].close (adjusted) - benchmark context, risk-match scaling regression and session calendar only; SPY is never a held leg

EW_SECTOR_TOTAL_RETURN equal-weight sector context derived from the same 11 {SYM}_all adjusted-close series per p2_a3_benchmark_contract.json membership and daily-rebalanced convention - used only in the sector-factor neutralization step
authorized_pit_inputs.fields_not_used: open, high, low, volume; the _none raw series (no price-level features used, raw-path authorization not exercised); distributions.json and split_factors.json (not needed on the _all path for S0); no fundamentals, earnings, borrow, short-interest, holdings, flows, options/implied-vol surfaces or intraday fields (all unavailable per data manifest; vov here is REALIZED, built only from daily closes)
authorized_pit_inputs.window_discipline: S0 screening/scoring window 2018-04-04..2025-07-31; the 252-session vov window at the first S0 decision is filled from the authorized pre-S0 runway (2010-01-04..2018-04-03) exactly as provided for warmup; no scored computation reads any session after 2025-07-31

universe_and_schedule.universe: all 11 SPDR sector ETFs of the frozen cohort (XLB, XLC, XLE, XLF, XLI, XLK, XLP, XLRE, XLU, XLV, XLY) - fixed non-cherry-picked rule: the full sector side of the frozen cohort, SPY excluded from legs (reserved as benchmark context per the frozen benchmark contract); a sector enters the ranking only when it has >= 252 sessions of authorized adjusted-close history (XLC from ~252 sessions after its 2018-06-19 inception, i.e., ~2019-06; before that it is excluded from ranks and held FLAT - an availability rule, not a selection)
universe_and_schedule.warmup_sessions: 252 sessions (exactly the maximum allowance); filled from authorized pre-S0 history so the first S0 session (2018-04-04) is already a valid decision tick
universe_and_schedule.decision_clock: every 21st SPY session (session-count clock, no calendar dependence); signals computed on session-t close data, PIT; the automaton re-seeds with the seed rule on the first tick of each S0 fold (force-flat boundaries respected)
universe_and_schedule.holding_period: 21 sessions (one clock period); weights held static between decision ticks; no intraperiod rebalancing
universe_and_schedule.fill_clock: next allowed session per baseline invariants (t+1 open-adjacent, close-to-close execution consistent with ADJ-1-EXEC-CLOCK; never a same-session fill)

anchor: ANCHOR SFV4-A4-H2-ANCHOR, exact rule (no parameter menu): (1) Returns r_{i,s} from adjusted closes of sector i on SPY-calendar sessions. (2) At each decision tick t, for each eligible sector: partition the trailing 252 sessions ending at t into 12 consecutive non-overlapping 21-session blocks (block 12 ends at t); block realized volatility v_k = sqrt(mean of squared daily returns within block k) (no demeaning, fixed convention); vov_i(t) = sample standard deviation (ddof=1) of the 12 values v_1..v_12. Rank eligible sectors by vov ASCENDING (rank 1 = lowest vov = most predictable risk); ties broken lexicographically by symbol. (3) Hysteresis book automaton over states LONG/SHORT/FLAT, evaluated only at ticks: seed (first tick of a fold): LONG := ranks 1-3, SHORT := ranks 9-11, others FLAT. Subsequent ticks, transitions applied in this fixed order: (i) exits - a LONG whose new rank >= 9 leaves LONG (to SHORT if |SHORT| < 3, else FLAT); a SHORT whose new rank <= 3 leaves SHORT (to LONG if |LONG| < 3, else FLAT); (ii) entries - FLAT sectors with rank <= 3 enter LONG in ascending-rank order while |LONG| < 3; FLAT sectors with rank >= 9 enter SHORT in descending-rank order while |SHORT| < 3; ties lexicographic. (4) Weights: +0.20 per LONG leg, -0.20 per SHORT leg; CASH absorbs the net residual; gross <= 1.2, net ~ 0; weights static between ticks. The rank-3/3, band <=3/>=9, 12x21-block, 252-session, 21-session-clock and 0.20 constants are fixed ex ante with no alternatives offered.
neighbour: SFV4-A4-H2-NEIGH, one fixed variant supporting the same mechanism: identical to the anchor in every element (3/3 hysteresis book, weights, clock, fill, universe, eligibility) except the vov statistic uses 6 consecutive non-overlapping 21-session blocks over the trailing 126 sessions (eligibility accordingly >= 126 sessions of history, XLC eligible from ~2018-12). Mechanism-support logic: uncertainty-about-risk is a property of the risk process at any reasonable memory length; if the mechanism is real, the shorter-memory neighbour carries the same sign with positive expectancy, and agreement of both arms supports the mechanism while disagreement marks the anchor as window-specific. No other variant is proposed.

causal_negative_control.control: SFV4-A4-H2-CTRL, realized-volatility LEVEL sort: identical surface form to the anchor (same 252-session window, same rank-and-hysteresis 3/3 book, same weights, clock, fills, universe, eligibility, sector-factor neutralization) but sectors are ranked by realized volatility LEVEL ascending, where level_i = sqrt(mean of squared daily returns over the trailing 252 sessions); LONG := ranks 1-3 (lowest vol), SHORT := ranks 9-11 (highest vol). If the causal story is true - that the priced object is the dispersion of the risk path (uncertainty about risk) and not the risk level - then after market neutralization and sector-factor removal a level-sort spread must NOT carry the premium: any documented level effect at single-name scale is a composite-level confound the vov claim explicitly does not rest on, and its presence would mean the anchor is reducible to the low-vol anomaly rather than vov pricing.
causal_negative_control.preregistered_falsification_rule: The anchor passes only if |control risk-matched incremental alpha| < 0.5 x anchor risk-matched incremental alpha AND control expectancy <= 0. If control expectancy > 0 or the ratio reaches 0.5 (frozen gate control_alpha_abs_ratio_lt = 0.5), the spread is attributed to a volatility-level effect and the anchor is rejected; no alternate control may be substituted after results are seen.

factor_alpha_test.risk_matched_incremental_alpha: Per the frozen benchmark contract: incremental_alpha(arm, window) = R_arm(window) - R_spy_context(window), with R_spy_context = SPY total return scaled EX ANTE by the arm's frozen scaling rule, never realized gross re-applied after the fact. This arm's frozen scaling rule (declared here, market-neutral book): kappa_t = clip(beta_hat_t, 0.0, 2.0), where beta_hat_t is the OLS slope of the arm's spread daily returns (a deterministic function of the frozen rule, hence PIT-computable at t) on SPY total-return daily returns over the trailing 252 sessions ending t-1. Evaluated per fold and overall; gates per frozen stage-A: anchor overall alpha > 0 and risk-matched excess positive folds >= 2.
factor_alpha_test.sector_factor_neutralization: Sector beta is plausible (all legs are sector ETFs), so the required neutralization step is added: OLS of the arm's daily returns on [SPY total return, EW_SECTOR total return] over each fold and over all of S0; the intercepts are reported annualized alongside the risk-matched context metric. A result whose intercept after both-factor removal is not positive fails the mechanism claim regardless of raw PnL.
factor_alpha_test.fail_closed: raw PnL, gross beta or long-equity exposure is never accepted as alpha; all gates fail closed per baseline invariants

costs_and_turnover.cost_model: 10 bps per side per fill at base, 20 bps per side at stress, charged exactly once per fill per baseline invariants
costs_and_turnover.expected_turnover: weights are static between monthly ticks and a 12-month volatility-of-volatility estimate is among the most persistent state statistics available from daily data, so band-crossing transitions are rare. Expected 0.5-2 swap events per side per year, each moving 0.20-0.60 of |delta w|: expected annualized two-way turnover ~0.8-2.0 (point estimate ~1.3), i.e., ~15-35% of the frozen 6.0 two-way/year ceiling. Cost drag ~13 bps/year at base, ~26 bps at stress. Two forced-flat fold-boundary events per cycle add negligible turnover.
costs_and_turnover.why_inside_ceiling: the design spends turnover only on genuine state transitions of an extremely persistent statistic; hysteresis bands plus the 12-month vov memory plus static weights between 21-session clocks structurally cap churn far below the ceiling with headroom for stress and boundary flattening

sample_size_floor.floors: >= 5 decisions/fold and >= 30 total are satisfied with large margin; early fold-1 ticks rank over 10 sectors until XLC reaches its 252-session eligibility (~2019-06), which reduces no tick count; at least 6 non-CASH legs are occupied at every tick, satisfying the min-positions invariant

drop_one_design.expected_max_concentration: 6 legs across 11 sectors with equal weights; ex ante no single sector should dominate spread contributions, but the honest hazard is a persistent single-sector bet (e.g., one defensive sector on the long side across an entire low-vov regime) pushing one ETF's positive contribution above the frozen etf_positive_share_le = 0.35 gate; this is treated as a live hazard, not assumed away
drop_one_design.drop_one_etf: value_book rerun excluding the max-contribution symbol per frozen convention; survival = after-drop expectancy > 0; meaningful because the claim is a cross-sectional premium - it must not be a single-pair artifact
drop_one_design.drop_one_fold: min over folds of expectancy with that fold removed; survival = min > 0; meaningful because risk-uncertainty premia can be single-regime artifacts (e.g., only the 2020 volatility episode), and the mechanism claims a persistent state premium, not one regime

failure_interpretation: A Stage-A reject means uncertainty-about-risk carries no exploitable after-cost, market-neutral cross-sectional premium in large liquid sector ETFs: either the Baltussen-class vov anomaly does not transfer from single stocks to sector composites, or whatever spread exists is absorbed by the volatility level (control gate) or by SPY/sector-factor exposure (neutralization gate). The mechanism class is thereby narrowed - risk-path uncertainty pricing fails at composite level - and no window, band or book tweak may be proposed to rescue it; a reject is terminal for this family in V4 and counts once in the historical denominator.

source_to_test_map.1: Baltussen-van Bekkum-van der Grient vov anomaly (high vov -> low subsequent returns) -> tradable direction: long lowest-vov, short highest-vov, market-neutral -> implemented as the ascending vov rank of the anchor
source_to_test_map.2: the priced object is dispersion of the risk path, distinct from the risk level (Ang-Hodrick-Xing-Zhang level benchmark) -> state variable vov_i = stdev of 12 non-overlapping 21-session block realized vols over trailing 252 sessions -> anchor step (2)
source_to_test_map.3: risk-uncertainty state variables carry return information (Bollerslev-Tauchen-Zhou, market-level strand) -> persistent state, monthly ticks, hysteresis entry/exit bands; no shock-triggered entries (shock reversal is a forbidden, separately rejected family) -> anchor step (3)
source_to_test_map.4: market/sector beta must not be mistaken for alpha -> net ~0 book + frozen kappa_t risk-matched SPY-context subtraction + [SPY, EW_SECTOR] intercept neutralization -> factor_alpha_test
source_to_test_map.5: if the mechanism is risk-path uncertainty, the vol level alone must not carry the spread -> level-sort control with preregistered 0.5 alpha-ratio and expectancy <= 0 falsification rule -> causal_negative_control
source_to_test_map.6: mechanism robustness across memory lengths -> 6-block/126-session neighbour must carry the same sign -> neighbour
source_to_test_map.7: survival after costs -> turnover bounded by hysteresis on an extremely persistent state; base and 20 bps stress reruns -> costs_and_turnover

implementation_estimate.engineer_days: ~3 days: nested-block vov signal module with per-symbol block alignment and PIT boundary checks (1.0), hysteresis automaton and bookkeeping reusing the H1 automaton pattern (0.75), control and neighbour arm configs (0.25), risk-match/sector-neutralization reporting (0.5), fold force-flat harness integration (0.5)
implementation_estimate.risk_notes: block alignment must be PIT-exact: the 12th block ends at the decision session t, no block may read past t, and per-symbol blocks must start at the symbol's own authorized history (XLC edge); eligibility thinning changes the rank pool mid-sample and must be logged; kappa_t trailing regression uses data through t-1 only (no leakage); vov and vol level are correlated - the control gate is the primary identification risk, acknowledged ex ante; all estimates here are analytic expectations, no PnL computed at proposal time
